zodiacus: The zodiac (pure Lat. orbis signifer), Cic. Arat. 317; Gell. 13, 9, 6.—Hence, zōdĭăcus, a, um, , of the zodiac: zodiacum diastema,Sid. Ep. 8, 11: zodiacus tractus,Mart. Cap. 1, § 44: zodiaca hospitia,id. ib. 1, § 5.
zoe: One of the Aeons of Valentinus, Tert. adv. Valent. 12.
zoilus: A severe critic in the time of Ptolemaeus Philadelphus, a censurer of Homer (hence called Ὁμηρομάστιξ, Homeromastix), Vitr. 7 praef.— Transf., of a censorious person, Ov. R. Am. 366; Mart. 11, 37, 1.
zomoteganite: A dish of fish stewed in their own liquor, Apic. 4, 2, § 147 dub.
zona: A belt, girdle, zone, worn about the loins by women (cf. cingulum).
· A girdle worn by men for containing money, a money-belt (cf. crumena), C. Gracch. ap. Gell. 15, 12 fin.; Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 40.
· The girdle or belt of Orion, a constellation, Ov. F. 6, 787.
· A line running around the edge of a gem, a girdle, Plin. 37, 6, 24, § 90.

· One of the imaginary circles which divided the earth into five climates, a zone, Verg. G. 1, 233; Ov. M. 1, 46; 2, 131; Plin. 2, 68, 68, § 172; Mel. 1, 1, 2; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 15, 13; 2, 5, 20; Mart. Cap. 6, § 602.
· A kind of herpes or erysipelas, which spreads about the body like a girdle, and destroys life, the shingles; called also zoster, Scrib. Comp. 63.
zonalis: Of or belonging to a zone (of the earth): ambitus,Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 5 med.
zonarius: Of or belonging to a belt or girdle.
Subst.: zōnārĭus, ii, m., a maker of girdles, Cic. Fl. 7, 17; Lucil. ap. Non. p. 2, 379 (Sat. Fr. 30, 16).
zonatim: Round about, in a circle, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 189, 33.
zone: A promontory of Thrace, opposite to Thasos, Mel. 2, 2; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 43.
zonula: A little girdle, Cat. 61, 53; Seren. ap. Non. p. 539, 19; Lampr. Alex. Sev. 52.
zoophorus: The frieze of a column (between the epistylium and the coronis), Vitr. 3, 5, 10; 4, 1, 2.
zoophthalmos: Great houseleek, called also aizoum majus, Plin. 25, 13, 102, § 160.
zopissa: Pitch mixed with wax, which was scraped off from ships, Plin. 16, 12, 23, § 56; 24, 7, 26, § 41.
zopyron: A plant, called also clinopodion, Plin. 24, 15, 87, § 137.
zopyrus: A celebrated physiognomist, Cic. Fat. 5, 10; id. Tusc. 4, 37, 80.
A Persian noble, who mutilated himself and thereby helped to conquer Babylon, Just. 1, 10, 15.
· · Zōpyriātim, , in the manner of Zopyrus, Lucil. ap. Non. p. 455, 17.
zoranisceos: A precious stone, otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 70, § 185.
zoroastres: Zoroaster, a lawgiver of the Medes, Just. 1, 1, 9; Plin. 30, 1, 2, § 3; App. Mag. p. 291.—Hence, Zōrŏ-astrēus, a, um, , of or belonging to Zoroaster, Zoroastrian: susurri,i. e. magical,Prud. Apoth. 494 (where Zŏr-, by solecism).
zoster: A kind of herpes, the shingles (cf. zona, II. E.), Plin. 26, 11, 74, § 121.
A kind of sca shrub (called also prason), Plin. 13, 25, 48, § 135.
A promontory, town, and harbor of Attica; the promontory is now called C. Lombarda, Cic. Att. 5, 12 init.
zotheca: A little private chamber, closet, or cabinet, for reposing in by day (cf. conclave), Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 21; cf. zothecula.
A recess, niche, for religious purposes, Inscr. Orell. 1368; 2006; 3889.
zothecula: A little closet or cabinet, Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 38; Sid. Ep. 8, 16; 9, 11.
zura: The seed of the Christ's-thorn (paliurus), Plin. 24, 13, 71, § 115.
zygia: zygĭa, ae, f., = ζυγία (prop. an  from ζύγιος, belonging to or fit for yokes)
A tree, called also carpinus, horn-beam: Carpinus betulus, Linn.; Plin. 16, 15, 26, § 67.
Zygia tibia, a nuptial or marriage flute, App. M. 4, p. 157, 37.
A name of Juno, as the goddess of marriage, App. M. 6, p. 174, 38.
zygostasium: The office of a weigh-master, Cod. Th. 15, 26, 1.
zygostates: A master of the weights, weigh-master, Cod. Th. 12, 7, 2; Cod. Just. 10, 71, 2.
zythum: A kind of malt-liquor among the Egyptians, Plin. 22, 25, 82, § 164; Col. 10, 116; Dig. 33, 6, 9 praef.
